scope: Sixteen assigned current-source declaration and bounded semantic reviews

files.how: Inspect the explicitly selected context, endpoint, engine and exact versions. Use fixed parallel reads and the separately qualified Windows stdio helper only for its admitted version tuple. Validate exact private inline Compose shape and resource labels before any owned mutation.
files.why: Ambient discovery, interpolated configuration or matching names alone cannot authorize adoption or stopping a resource.
files.tradeoffsOrLimits: The qualified Windows helper and native CLI paths differ; inspection is not TLS authentication. The lock-held flag requires a real caller-owned OS lease and is not independently granted by this adapter.
files.evidenceLimit: Earlier admission findings and their repairs have different source hashes. They remain historical; no new engine run or current whole-platform acceptance is inferred.
files.proposedReviewStatus: P02 bounded current-source/declaration review only; historical runtime evidence remains separate and native/phase acceptance is open

files.how: Retain an existing private profile directory descriptor, open the hashed lock with no-follow, nonblocking and close-on-exec flags, check held descriptor access and recheck directory/file identity after flock before writing a random attempt marker.
files.where: AcquireBootstrapLock lines 56-152; held access checks at 83, 105 and 131; Close lines 156-163.
files.why: Prevent permissive access or replaced path identity from authorizing the startup lease. The lock inode is never unlinked, and observed metadata cannot authorize takeover.
files.tradeoffsOrLimits: Canonical ancestry remains an enrollment prerequisite. Ordinary filesystem calls are synchronous; a finite context does not preempt them. An already canceled context is checked in the lock loop, not before every filesystem effect. The original lock-only evidence binds a different source hash.

files.how: Use a typed authority sentinel, safe stage diagnostics and an optional private operation proof. Owned transport cleanup precedes NATS Close and invalidates a successful snapshot on failure.
files.where: Authority/stage declarations lines 31-67; observeKernelWithProof lines 159-325, authority 180-213, cleanup 218-226 and secure dialer 227-249.
files.why: Avoid redundant inspection within one authorized observation without substituting cached claims for TLS or readiness. Preserve authority and concrete cleanup errors while exposing only fixed diagnostics.
files.tradeoffsOrLimits: The nil-trust standalone prototype branch remains plaintext; installed admission is a separate prerequisite. The proof implementation and installed loader are outside these eight files. Snapshot freshness is decoded rather than retimestamped. Final-stage historical review matches this file hash but its raw execution was not re-audited here.

findings.title: Startup failure cause is lost when cleanup also fails
findings.description: After a concrete startup error, Start calls g.Stop. If Stop fails, line 333 wraps only cleanupErr and discards err. A caller can retain the returned exact Group and inspect the cleanup failure, but cannot recover the original canceled/deadline/pre-spawn/start cause through errors.Is or errors.As on the returned error. This is a source-proven diagnostic limitation of the dual-failure branch, not a claim that an actual native run failed.
findings.nextAction: Root should retain both operational and cleanup causes while preserving the exact Group and existing cleanup ownership/budgets, or explicitly track this limitation. Do not describe this branch as preserving the original startup cause.
findings.executionEvidence: None collected by this reviewer. No reproduction was run.
